topics.title: What Is System Design?
topics.description: What a system is, why design matters at scale, the bank-counter story of scaling, and the three failures of a single cheap server.

topics.title: HLD vs LLD

topics.title: Functional and Non-Functional Requirements
topics.description: What the system does vs how well it does it, the standard quality attributes, and why qualities decide the architecture.

topics.title: Clarifying Requirements
topics.description: The questions to ask before drawing anything: users, read/write mix, what must never be lost, latency budget and cost.

topics.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
topics.description: Turning users into requests per second, peak load, storage, bandwidth and replica counts with round numbers.

topics.title: SLA, SLO, SLI and Availability Math
topics.description: Indicators, objectives and agreements, what the nines mean in downtime, error budgets, and availability of serial and parallel components.

topics.title: Data-Intensive vs Compute-Intensive Systems
topics.description: Deciding whether time is lost moving data or calculating, and why that decides where you spend effort and money.

topics.title: The Building Blocks of a System
topics.description: Clients, application servers and APIs, databases, caches, load balancers, queues, storage and monitoring, plus sync vs async calls.

topics.title: Monolith, Modular Monolith and Microservices
topics.description: One deployable, one deployable with strict modules, or many services: what each costs and when to split.

topics.title: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling

topics.title: Stateless vs Stateful Services

topics.title: The Journey of a Request

topics.title: DNS in System Design
topics.description: How names become addresses, why DNS is distributed and cached, and how TTLs and DNS routing are used for failover and geography.

topics.title: IP Addresses, Ports, Sockets and Connections
topics.description: Addresses find a machine, ports find a process, a socket pair identifies a connection, and why connections are a limited resource.

topics.title: HTTP and HTTPS for System Design
topics.description: Requests, responses, methods and headers, what TLS adds, keep-alive, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, and where TLS is terminated.

topics.title: REST API Design

topics.title: Reverse Proxy and API Gateway
topics.description: Forward vs reverse proxies, what an API gateway adds for microservices, and how both relate to load balancers.

topics.title: Content Delivery Networks (CDN)

topics.title: Service Discovery
topics.description: How services find healthy instances of each other when addresses change: registries, client- and server-side discovery, DNS.

topics.title: Data Modeling and Access Patterns
topics.description: Starting from the questions users ask the system, then shaping records and keys to answer them, before picking technology.

topics.title: Relational Databases in System Design
topics.description: Tables, keys, constraints and relationships, ACID transactions, and what relational databases do well and badly at scale.

topics.title: NoSQL Databases
topics.description: Key-value, document, wide-column and graph databases: data models, strengths, limits, and what "NoSQL scales" really means.

topics.title: Choosing a Database
topics.description: A reasoning process for picking storage from access patterns, relationships, consistency, scale and operations, with worked decisions.

topics.title: Database Indexes at Scale

topics.title: Connection Pooling and Database Bottlenecks
topics.description: Why opening connections is expensive, connection limits, pool sizing, and the usual ways a database becomes the bottleneck.

topics.title: Object and Blob Storage

topics.title: Search Systems
topics.description: Why LIKE queries do not scale, inverted indexes, relevance, and running Elasticsearch or OpenSearch beside the main database.

topics.title: Caching Fundamentals

topics.title: Cache Invalidation and TTL

topics.title: Cache Stampede, Penetration and Hot Keys
topics.description: The three ways a cache fails under load: many misses at once, misses that never fill, and one key too hot for one node.

topics.title: Distributed Caching
topics.description: Local vs shared caches, partitioning a cache across nodes, replication and failover, and two-level caching.

topics.title: Load Balancing Fundamentals

topics.title: Load-Balancing Algorithms

topics.title: Database Replication and Read Replicas

topics.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Replication and Lag

topics.title: Multi-Leader and Leaderless Replication

topics.title: Quorum Reads and Writes

topics.title: Sharding and Partitioning

topics.title: Hot Partitions, Resharding and Secondary Indexes

topics.title: Consistent Hashing

topics.title: Capacity Planning and Finding Bottlenecks
topics.description: Turning estimates into machine counts with headroom, finding the component that limits throughput, and load testing.

topics.title: The CAP Theorem

topics.title: Strong vs Eventual Consistency

topics.title: Distributed Locks and Leader Election

topics.title: Distributed Transactions, Sagas and the Outbox

topics.title: Failures and Single Points of Failure

topics.title: Redundancy, High Availability and Failover

topics.title: Timeouts, Retries, Backoff and Jitter

topics.title: Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads and Fallbacks

topics.title: Idempotency

topics.title: Graceful Degradation and Load Shedding

topics.title: Disaster Recovery, Backups, RPO and RTO

topics.title: Point-to-Point Queues vs Publish-Subscribe

topics.title: Delivery Semantics: At-Most-Once, At-Least-Once, Exactly-Once

topics.title: Message Ordering, Partitions and Consumer Groups
topics.description: Why global ordering does not scale, per-key ordering with partitions, and how consumer groups share work.

topics.title: Dead-Letter and Retry Queues
topics.description: Handling messages that keep failing: retry limits, delayed retry queues, dead-letter queues and redriving.

topics.title: Backpressure
topics.description: What to do when producers are faster than consumers: bounded queues, signalling upstream, scaling consumers and shedding.

topics.title: Kafka vs RabbitMQ
topics.description: A replayable partitioned log vs a routing message broker: models, strengths, and how to pick one in an interview.

topics.title: Event-Driven Architecture
topics.description: Services reacting to events instead of calling each other: events vs commands, choreography vs orchestration, and the costs.

topics.title: Observability: Metrics, Logs and Traces
topics.description: The three signals for understanding a running system, structured logging, correlation IDs and what to measure first.

topics.title: Latency Percentiles: P50, P95, P99

topics.title: Distributed Tracing
topics.description: Following one request across services with traces and spans, context propagation, sampling, and finding the slow hop.

topics.title: Monitoring and Alerting
topics.description: The four golden signals, RED and USE, API and machine metrics, alerting on symptoms and error budgets, and avoiding alert fatigue.

topics.description: Requirements to final architecture for a short-link service: estimation, APIs, ID generation, storage, caching, redirects and failures.

topics.title: Case Study: Design a Photo-Sharing App

topics.title: Case Study: Design a Video Streaming Platform
topics.description: Upload, transcoding pipeline, segments and adaptive bitrate, HLS and DASH over HTTP, CDNs and the numbers behind them.

topics.title: Case Study: Design a Chat Application
topics.description: One-to-one and group messaging: persistent connections, routing between servers, ordering, delivery receipts, offline users and presence.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Data and Caching
topics.description: Mixed interview bank across data modeling, database choice, indexes, storage, search and every caching topic.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Scaling and Consistency
topics.description: Mixed interview bank across load balancing, replication, sharding, consistent hashing, CAP, consistency and coordination.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Reliability, Messaging and Operations
topics.description: Mixed interview bank across failures, retries, circuit breakers, idempotency, DR, queues, delivery semantics and observability.

topics.description: Production-style "what happens if" and "the system is slow" questions that combine several topics in one answer.
